subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Having a chip on one’s shoulder

options.text: Having an unnecessary feeling of guilt
Having an irritated and unfriendly attitude
Having a proud and self-centred arrogance
Showing great resistance to any adversities

solution:
The correct answer is: **Having an irritated and unfriendly attitude.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom "**having a chip on one's shoulder**" means to be easily offended or to have a confrontational attitude. (आसानी से नाराज हो जाना या टकरावपूर्ण रवैया अपनाना)
 
• This idiom comes from the practice of placing a chip of wood on one's shoulder and daring others to knock it off as a sign of readiness for a fight.
 
• Someone with a chip on their shoulder may feel that they have been wronged or unfairly treated in the past, leading to their defensive or hostile behaviour.
 
 
• **Examples**:
 
 
• *Ever since he got passed over for that promotion, he's had a real chip on his shoulder.*
 
• *Don't take it personally - she just has a chip on her shoulder about everything.*
 
 
 
 

Therefore, **option 2** is the correct answer.
